## Why Morrison Rich authoring is the single next priority

The UI spine is wired. Every route resolves, every tier component renders, every cross-link traverses. The spine is now ready to hold real content. Morrison is the program Prat clicks through during the demo — every deliverable he opens must read as decision-grade, not template-filler. Until Morrison is end-to-end Rich, the demo has a weak link somewhere along the golden path.

44 Rich deliverables total across three hero programs. Morrison's 14 are the highest-leverage subset because they anchor the primary click-path. Ambient (MRD-01) and Demand Forecasting (APX-02) follow in priority order.

## What "Rich fidelity" means (the 12-component contract)

Every Rich deliverable must render all 12 required components from Part 3.1 of the seed spec. D17 is the canonical exemplar — match its structural pattern, not its content. Per-deliverable checklist:

1. **Executive summary block** (80-120 words) — Georgia serif, 19px, teal-accented card, anchored on the outcome. Reads as the "80-word version" the CXO sees if they read nothing else.
2. **KPI strip** — 4 cards, Georgia serif numeric values, mono caps labels, DM Sans delta lines. Values must be tenant-specific and numerically coherent (don't overclaim; don't default to round numbers).
3. **Narrative body** (800-1,500 words) — H2/H3 section headers, populated prose, not bullets as a substitute for writing. Inline evidence citation chips (E1, E2, E3 styling from D17) wherever a numeric claim is made.
4. **Data table** — at least one tenant-specific table with sortable columns. Preferred rows highlighted teal where applicable (e.g., preferred suppliers, primary options).
5. **Inline chart** — SVG where appropriate (projections, timelines, distributions). Match D17's chart styling (teal + teal-dark ramp, amber breakeven markers, mono axis labels).
6. **Decision log extract** — 3-5 dated decisions leading up to this deliverable, with teal mono dates.
7. **Risks and mitigations** (Phase 3+) — 2-3 risks with High/Med/Critical tier chips, prose explanation, mitigation line.
8. **Tenant bindings resolved** — every `{{}}` placeholder resolved. No unresolved tokens anywhere. Every number, name, percentage tenant-specific to Apex Retail / Morrison.
9. **Breadcrumbs** — full chain: Apex Retail Group › Programs › Morrison Owned Brand Margin Recovery › Phase N › DNN.
10. **Cross-links sidebar** — 4 sections: On this page (anchor nav), Cross-links (source pattern, prerequisite, downstream), Evidence base (interviews, baseline, benchmark, models), Analogous programs.
11. **Print CSS** — renders cleanly in browser print preview. Navbar, sidebar, actions, footer hidden. Main body + KPI strip + data table + chart visible.
12. **Provenance footer** — "Generated by Nexus on {date} · Grounded in N evidence sources · Last updated {timestamp}." Plus the composite disclaimer line.

Integrity layer is non-negotiable on every Rich deliverable: composite disclaimer ("composite organization built from real-world data") + demo-rendering disclaimer ("this document is a demo rendering, not a deliverable for a real engagement") in the footer.

## Authoring workflow per deliverable

For each deliverable, follow this sequence:

1. **Copy the D17 HTML structure** as the starting template. Preserve all 12 components; swap the content.
2. **Populate the YAML/front-matter** with deliverable code, phase, tier, tenant, program, status.
3. **Write the executive summary first** — force the authoring discipline of "if the CFO reads only this, what do they know?" 80-120 words, Georgia serif treatment.
4. **Fill the KPI strip** — 4 tenant-specific KPIs with numeric coherence across the deliverable.
5. **Author the narrative body** — H2/H3 structure, 800-1,500 words, inline evidence citations (E1, E2, ...) where numeric claims appear.
6. **Build the data table** — real tenant-specific rows, preferred highlighting where applicable.
7. **Author the chart** as inline SVG — use D17's chart as styling reference (teal ramp, mono labels, subtle grid).
8. **Write the decision log** — 3-5 dated decisions leading to this deliverable, teal mono dates.
9. **Author risks** (Phase 3+ only) — 2-3 risks with tier chips and mitigation lines.
10. **Wire the cross-links sidebar** — on-page anchors, source pattern link, prerequisite + downstream deliverables, evidence base, analogous programs.
11. **Verify tenant bindings** — every `{{}}` resolved; no unresolved tokens.
12. **Verify integrity footer** — composite disclaimer + demo-rendering disclaimer + provenance line.
13. **Spot-check print CSS** — browser print preview renders cleanly.
14. **Validate against integrity tests** — tier contract test, cross-link class test, route resolution test.

Per deliverable: ~25-40 minutes of Claude Code work assuming the D17 template is clean. Across 14 deliverables: approximately 6-9 hours of focused authoring, parallelizable across Claude Code instances.

## Content authoring guardrails (non-negotiable)

From Part 7 of the wireframes doc:

- **Every supplier named `Supplier A/B/C`** — never real company names. Anonymization discipline.
- **Every stakeholder name composite** — Marcus T. CFO, Katherine P. CMO, Diane R. SVP Supply Chain, etc. Use consistent first-name-last-initial format.
- **Every percentage, dollar amount, date tenant-specific** — no generic placeholder numbers.
- **Composite disclaimer + demo-rendering disclaimer** in every deliverable footer.
- **No claim of attested outcomes** — all financial projections framed as "projected," "target," "at steady state."
- **Evidence citations must resolve** — if `E1` is referenced inline, there must be an E1 entry in the evidence base sidebar.

## Priority order and sequencing recommendation

Author in the following sequence to maximize demo-readiness at each checkpoint:

**Tier A — first (demo-critical spine):**
1. D01 Charter · D03 Success Metric Tree — demo opens on Morrison; charter and metric tree are the first things Prat sees
2. D07 Financial Baseline · D09 RCA — prove the problem is real
3. D15 Intervention Portfolio · D16 Business Case — prove the solution is priced
4. D19 Delivery Plan — prove execution is organized

**Tier B — second (depth for scrolling):**
5. D02 Stakeholder Map · D04 Intake Synthesis — Phase 1 depth
6. D08 Pain Points · D10 Benchmark · D11 Hypotheses — Phase 2 depth
7. D12 Roadmap · D18 Risk Register — Phase 3 depth

**Tier C — third (build-phase depth):**
8. D20 Sprint Artifacts · D22 Change Management · D24 Outcome Measurement Plan

If demo timing forces cuts, Tier A alone (7 deliverables) plus the existing D17 gives Prat a complete decision-narrative. Tiers B and C increase depth for unscripted drill-downs.

## Acceptance criteria

A Morrison Rich deliverable is considered complete when:

- [ ] All 12 Rich components render per the contract
- [ ] Integrity test suite passes on the deliverable
- [ ] Cross-link generator resolves all 8 cross-link classes correctly
- [ ] Tenant bindings resolved (linter reports zero `{{}}` or unresolved tokens)
- [ ] Composite disclaimer + demo-rendering disclaimer present in footer
- [ ] Print CSS validated in browser print preview
- [ ] Manual walk from Morrison program page → this deliverable succeeds
- [ ] Back navigation and cross-links resolve without 404s
- [ ] Anand review pass
